metaTitle: Soma — Educational models of physiological recovery
metaDescription: Soma is an educational web app for modelled physiological recovery after substance use. Try the demo without an account. Curves are estimates, not diagnoses.

hero.subtitle: Soma visualizes orientative trajectories from scientific literature and a personal timeline. They are educational estimates from catalog curves — not clinical measurements, diagnoses, or a guarantee of individual recovery.
hero.ctaInviteNote: Soma is in public beta. Sign-up currently requires an invitation. If you were invited, use the link you received.
hero.disclaimer: Educational models. Soma is not a medical device. Panels in the artwork are visual motifs, not measurements or profile data.

features.title: What you can explore in Soma today
features.intro: An educational and motivational tool for understanding what happens in the body after stopping a substance. Every area can be explored in the demo, without an account.
features.note: The models are educational estimates from the catalog. Soma does not diagnose, is not a medical device, and does not predict your personal recovery.

recovery.title: Recovery
recovery.body: Educational curves by system and abstinence clocks based on your timeline.

neurotransmitters.title: Neurotransmitters
neurotransmitters.body: Nine qualitative, educational profiles. They do not measure your brain activity.

substances.title: Substance explorer
substances.body: Alcohol, nicotine, cannabis, cocaine and caffeine: educational sheets, processes and phases.

atlas.title: Anatomical atlas
atlas.body: Twelve body systems on illustrated plates.

journal.title: Journal
journal.body: A personal, voluntary space to record mood, sleep, energy and notes.

missions.title: Educational missions
missions.body: Short readings with questions that add experience when completed.

achievements.title: Achievements and levels
achievements.body: Medals tied to catalog thresholds, experience, levels and titles.

expedition.title: Expedition centre
expedition.body: Knowledge and perseverance routes on an interactive map.

journey.title: Recovery does not happen overnight.
journey.subtitle: Each physiological process has its own pace. Soma helps you explore orientative trajectories grounded in scientific literature and understand how different systems in the body can evolve.
journey.chartTitle: Illustrative curve. Not a Soma catalog trajectory.
journey.hint: Drag the control or use the arrow keys.
journey.caption: Conceptual demonstration. The shape of the line is not calibrated, not taken from Soma’s scientific catalog, and not a clinical prediction.

atlas.title: Explore the Human Body
atlas.subtitle: Choose a physiological system to see where it sits in the body. The plates highlight structures; they do not measure or predict recovery.
atlas.overviewBody: Anterior view of the body. Select a system to highlight its structures on this reference.
atlas.emptySystem: This plate illustrates the system. The catalog does not list canonical organs here.
atlas.disclaimer: Educational anatomical illustrations. They are not clinical measurements or recovery predictions.
atlas.plateAltSystem: {{name}} highlighted on the body in anterior view.

blurbs.nervous-central: Brain and spinal cord, the body’s axis of integration.
blurbs.cardiovascular: Heart and vessels that drive and distribute blood.
blurbs.respiratory: Airways and lungs that allow gas exchange.
blurbs.digestive: Digestive tract that processes food. The liver may also appear; the hepatic system has its own plate.
blurbs.immune: A network of vessels, nodes and lymphatic organs, including the spleen.
blurbs.hepatic: Liver and biliary tract, central to metabolism.
blurbs.renal: Kidneys and urinary tract that filter blood and help regulate the internal environment.
blurbs.reproductive: Reproductive system. The full-body plate shows male anatomy.
blurbs.integumentary: Skin and cutaneous appendages, the body’s outer boundary.
blurbs.sensory: Sense organs visible in the anterior view.
blurbs.endocrine: Glands that release hormones into the blood and coordinate distant functions.
blurbs.nervous-peripheral: Nerves and ganglia outside the brain and spinal cord.

science.title: From literature to an educational trajectory.
science.subtitle: Evidence suggests a shape and parameters. The continuous stroke is mathematical interpolation, not a measurement of you.

research.title: Research
research.body: Literature and, when they exist, guidelines: which structures, what pace, and how much confidence. It does not measure the user.

modeling.title: Educational modeling
modeling.body: Shape, horizon, and ceiling. Between anchors the curve is interpolated: a point on the stroke is not a data point from a study.

exploration.title: Exploration
exploration.body: The demo or your timeline places the catalog on days. It is estimated advance, not a biomarker or a diagnosis.

logarithmic.title: Logarithmic
logarithmic.body: More change early on, then it flattens. Used when the literature describes an early gain that then slows.

sigmoidal.title: Sigmoidal
sigmoidal.body: Starts slowly, accelerates, then flattens again. Fits processes that take time to get going and then stabilize.

linear.title: Linear
linear.body: Steady advance in the model. Reserved for when the data do not justify another shape; discrete milestones are still drawn as a continuous approximation.

science.shapesCaption: Illustrative glyphs. They are not clinical curves and not a catalog trajectory drawn to scale.
science.confidenceIntro: Each catalog pair carries a confidence level. It describes how strong the sources are — not a statistical probability and not certainty about an individual outcome.

high.title: High
high.body: Broad consensus, several longitudinal studies, or established guidelines. The model is still a simplification.

medium.title: Medium
medium.body: Solid literature, with person-to-person variability or limited samples. Uncertainty stays in view.

low.title: Low
low.body: Emerging evidence, preliminary studies, or extrapolation. It should not be read as a settled clinical fact.

science.notice: Educational catalog models. They are not clinical measurements or the end of recovery.
science.limits: The curves are educational trajectories parameterized from the catalog: they are not validated clinical averages, and they are not personal measurements or individual prognoses. The model does not fully incorporate individual variability, comorbidities, or interactions between substances. Internal scales are for visualization, not medical percentages. Not every catalog reference has been verified against the primary source. Soma is not a medical device.

methodology.title: How to read the model.
methodology.subtitle: Each shape describes an interpolation pattern. Confidence speaks to the sources. The limits recall what the model cannot claim.

origin.title: Why Soma?
origin.p1: Our organism is in constant transformation. Even when we are not aware of it, extraordinary processes take place within.
origin.p2: Soma is born of the will to make those changes visible and understandable, bringing the science of recovery closer to those who want to understand what happens in their body.
origin.p3: Because understanding what happens inside us can also help us make sense of the path we are walking.

path.title: Every step counts. Every story matters.

missions.title: Missions
missions.subtitle: Small challenges, real progress
missions.body: Put what you have learned to the test. Missions invite you to explore how your organism works through small educational challenges. Answer correctly and gain experience as you broaden your knowledge.
missions.note: Illustrative examples from the real catalog. They are not your progress.

journal.title: Journal
journal.subtitle: Your story matters too
journal.body: Recovery is also made of experiences, thoughts and small discoveries. The Journal is a personal space to record and remember your path.
journal.sampleBody: Today I could name what I felt without turning it into a diagnosis. Just a note so I do not lose the thread.
journal.note: Fictional notes. They do not belong to any account.
journal.demo: See the journal in the demo

expedition.title: Your journey, on a map you can explore.
expedition.badge: Available now in the public beta
expedition.intro: The Expedition centre is an educational, interactive experience. It brings together on an illustrated map what already exists in Soma: you choose a stage, see its progress and open the matching section to keep exploring and progress through missions.

knowledge.title: Knowledge routes
knowledge.body: Five stages — neuroscience, anatomy, substances, key processes and recovery — connected to the educational missions and the sections of Soma.

perseverance.title: Perseverance routes
perseverance.body: One stage per substance, with the abstinence milestones from your timeline. The clock follows abstinence, not sign-ins.

expedition.demo: Explore the expedition in the demo
expedition.mapAlt: Illustrated map of the Soma Expedition centre: a landscape with five beacons marking the stages of the journey.
expedition.mapCaption: The real expedition map artwork. In the app, the beacons show the state of each stage.
expedition.note: In the demo the figures are examples; with an account, the expedition uses your data. It is an educational and motivational journey, not a clinical assessment or a prediction of your recovery.

achievements.title: Every step deserves to be recognized.
achievements.intro: Soma recognizes milestones tied to thresholds in its educational models. This showcase displays real catalog pieces, not personal progress.
achievements.sealedBody: Some achievements stay sealed until they are reached. This showcase does not reveal the name or the description.
achievements.note: Achievements are granted when a modeled educational trajectory crosses a catalog threshold. They are not clinical measurements, and not proof that an organ has recovered.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Brief answers about what Soma is and what it is not. They do not replace the terms of use or the privacy policy.

what.question: What is Soma?
what.answer: Soma is an educational and motivational web app for adults (18+) who want to explore, at their own pace, how an educational catalog describes some physiological changes linked to abstinence and recovery. It visualizes orientative trajectories and offers learning tools (atlas, missions, journal, expedition, and more). It is not a healthcare provider, not a medical device, and it does not diagnose or treat.

curves.question: Do the curves represent my personal recovery?
curves.answer: No. The curves and clocks are educational catalog models: orientative estimates grounded in literature and product rules, placed on a timeline. They do not measure your body, read biomarkers, or guarantee an individual outcome. A point on a curve is not a clinical data point about you.
curves.learnMore: More detail on the educational models

care.question: Does Soma replace medical or psychological care?
care.answer: No. Soma is an educational companion. It does not diagnose, prescribe, or replace health professionals or emergency services. If there is immediate danger or you need clinical care, contact the health resources in your area.

demo.question: What can I explore without creating an account?
demo.answer: The demo lets you browse educational surfaces of the product without signing up: illustrative recovery, the explorer (substances and neurotransmitters), atlas, missions, achievements, expedition and sample journal. Demo sample data does not belong to any real account. Creating an account (when you have an invitation) enables personalized use according to the product’s features and consents; it is not required to learn what Soma is.

beta.question: Is Soma free during the beta?
beta.answer: Yes. In the public beta, access is offered without payment, advertising or subscription, according to the current legal texts. General sign-up is not open: an invitation is required. A free beta does not promise an indefinite duration or a recovery outcome.

closing.title: Your journey starts today.
closing.subtitle: Every day is part of a larger story. Discover how to explore your evolution, understand the processes in your body, and recognize the milestones along the way.
closing.ctaInviteNote: General sign-up is not open: an invitation is required. Soma remains in public beta.
closing.note: Orientative educational models. They do not replace a medical evaluation.
closing.tagline: Understanding recovery, one day at a time.
